task_description: Designing new superalloys with improved γ₀-phase solvus temperature (Tγ₀) via extrapolation from sparse data—specifically, identifying chemically distinct alloy compositions predicted to increase Tγ₀ by ~50 °C relative to known superalloys, using limited initial data and minimal experimental validation.

datasets.db_description: A curated dataset of 179 experimentally measured superalloys with reported γ₀-phase solvus temperature (Tγ₀), comprising 106 Co-base, 42 Co–Ni-base, and 31 Ni-base compositions. Each entry includes 64 compositional and physicochemical features (e.g., atomic radius deviations, mixing enthalpy, thermal expansion mismatch) derived from elemental properties. This dataset is used to train and validate the gradient boosting regression surrogate model for predicting Tγ₀ and to inform interpretable feature analysis (e.g., SHAP) guiding search space reduction and extrapolation.

A binary-labeled dataset of 254 superalloys indicating presence (221 samples) or absence (33 samples) of the γ₀ phase, used to train a random forest classification model. It supports the task by enabling high-throughput screening of candidate alloys generated in the search space to retain only those thermodynamically and structurally likely to form the strengthening γ₀ phase—thus constraining the vast compositional space to physically viable candidates before unsupervised sampling.
